ordered_diagnoses: Corrected transposition of the great arteries

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with vomiting and abnormal cardiac findings
salient_findings: Chest pain and vomiting
Elevated serum troponin I level
ST-segment elevations in multiple ECG leads
Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Abnormal cardiac anatomy with right atrium and ventricle on the left side
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 80s
Chest pain duration is 1 hour
Patient denies history of hypertension and diabetes
Temperature is 36°C
Heart rate is 79 beats per minute
Blood pressure is 92/56 mm Hg
Maximal cardiac impulse is in the right fifth interspace
Hepatic dullness is located in the left subcostal region
Initial serum troponin I level is 0.070 ng/mL
ECG shows negative P waves in lead I and ST-segment elevations in multiple leads
Coronary Angiography shows total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Transthoracic Echocardiogram shows abnormal cardiac anatomy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, vomiting, elevated serum troponin I level, and ST-segment elevations in multiple ECG leads, along with the total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery seen on coronary angiography, are all consistent with an acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
rejected.why: While the patient has an abnormal cardiac anatomy, the key findings of chest pain, elevated troponin, and coronary occlusion point more directly to a myocardial infarction than to a congenital condition like dextrocardia with situs inversus.

rejected.label: Corrected transposition of the great arteries
rejected.why: This congenital condition does not directly explain the acute presentation of chest pain and elevated troponin levels.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the vignette that points to arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy as the primary cause of the patient's symptoms and findings.

rejected.label: Coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: While coronary artery dissection could lead to myocardial infarction, the provided information does not specifically indicate dissection, and the total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery is more directly suggestive of a thrombotic event leading to acute myocardial infarction.
